newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmaker wants major Senate debate on Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmaker wants major Senate debate on Fed.

text.p: Sen. Tom Harkin criticized Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan Thursday for not promoting economic growth and said he wants a big debate on money policy when the Senate considers President Clinton's Fed nominees.
"Americans need a more growth-oriented Federal Reserve," the Iowa Democrat said in a statement. "For too long, this Greenspan Fed has restrained growth."
Clinton said earlier that he would nominate University of Michigan professor Edward Gramlich and economic consultant Roger Ferguson to the central bank's board.

"No Fed nominee should be rubber-stamped by the Senate," Harkin said. "I look forward to a substantive debate on monetary policy and a more growth-oriented Fed on the Senate floor during the nomination process."
Harkin forced a lengthy Senate debate on Fed policy last year before acceding to a vote on Greenspan's nomination to a third term as Fed Chairman.
